value.Title: Massachusetts Division of Banks issues a Regulatory Notice regarding Money Transmitter Licensing Requirements
value.NewsItemDescription:
July 31, 2026: Regulatory Notice: Reminder of Money Transmitter Licensing Requirements under MGL c. 169B

The Division of Banks began accepting money transmitter license applications through NMLS on July 1, 2025. All entities engaged in money transmission activities under Massachusetts General Laws chapter 169B were required to submit an application for a money transmitter license through the NMLS by July 1, 2026, unless the entity was licensed as a Foreign Transmittal Agency and/or a Check Seller with an approved license as of Dec. 31, 2025. Those entities transitioned to the new money transmitter license by filing a transition request through the NMLS during the NMLS renewal period starting Nov. 1, 2025. ​

As a reminder, any person or entity that is required to obtain a money transmitter license under MGL c. 169B and did not submit an application on or before July 1, 2026, must immediately cease all licensable activity and is prohibited from engaging in money transmission activity in Massachusetts unless and until the required license has been granted.  Failure to obtain any required license under MGL c. 169B, could subject any person or entity to penalties, including the imposition of civil penalties under MGL c. 169B, §10.

value.Title: Notice Regarding Recent Assessment Invoices for Maryland Mortgage Lender Licensees
value.NewsItemDescription:
The Maryland Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) discovered a typographical error in the description of the formula used to calculate the assessment of Maryland mortgage lender licensees and seeks to assure licensees that this error does not change the assessment amounts.

The formula description referred to “the total dollar amount you provided on MD MCR line AC990 for each quarter of 2024” (emphasis added). The reference to 2024 was incorrect. The correct statement for this portion of the assessment methodology is, “the total dollar amount you provided on MD MCR line AC990 for each quarter of 2025.”  The typo did not affect any calculations related to the assessment amounts, which are accurate and based on 2025 data. MD OFR apologizes for any confusion this may have caused.

For questions about this advisory, please contact Assistant Commissioner Clifford Charland at clifford.charland@maryland.gov.

value.Title: Nevada Division of Mortgage Lending Enacts Cyber Security Program and Breach Reporting Requirements
value.NewsItemDescription: The Nevada Division of Mortgage Lending announces amendments to NRS 645B, NRS 645F, & NRS 645A requiring licensees to comply with the requirements set forth in 16 C.F.R. value.Title: Indiana Requires Quarterly Reporting for Earned Wage Access License Applicants & Licensees
value.NewsItemDescription:
All EWA providers should begin tracking Indiana transactions as of January 1, 2026. Quarterly reports are due 45 days after the closing date of each quarter:  
  • ​Q1: May 15 
  • Q2: August 14 
  • Q3: November 14 
  • Q4: February 14 
The Excel template identifying all required data to be included in the report can be found on the IN-DFI website, HERE.  The Quarterly Report should be uploaded to the Additional Requirements section of the Document Uploads in NMLS.  If the file size is too large or the licensee prefers, the report may be submitted via secure email to DFIlicensing@dfi.in.gov​.

value.Title: Colorado Model Money Transmission Modernization Act Effective Aug. 6
value.NewsItemDescription: Colorado Governor Polis signed the Money Transmitter Model Act into law on Friday, April 18, 2025; it becomes effective 90 days from the closing of the legislature, which makes the effective date August 6, 2025. Applicants and licensees will be required to meet specific tangible net worth and other financial requirements. Additionally, updates will be made to the Electronic Surety Bond and NMLS settings and checklists. Furthermore, statutory exemptions to licensing are now included for payroll processors and "agent-of-the-payee" business models. Please review the full law (HB25-1201) for updates and changes applicable to your institution.  If you have any questions, please contact the Division of Banking at 303-894-7575 or DORA_BankingWebsite@state.co.us.
